This is Manau. Ancient roots / contemporary.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: According to legend, Jingpo people came down from the mountain, Majoi Shingra, to Hkranghku Majoi before celebrating Manaus.
Between AD. 300 and 400, Jawa Rumja, the son of Pawng Yawng, married a Lamu madai girl, after which Lamu madai led the first Manau.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The biggest manau dance, the sut manau, is held in January, though manaus can be held throughout the year.
The ceremony has roots in animistic religion despite the majority of Kachin people being Christian.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: A senior official leads a procession of dancers in circles around the sacred manau poles.
Male dancers hold a traditional Kachin sword called an n'htu during the dance.
Watch for Procession around manau poles.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The ceremony takes place on the manau ground, the cultural center of Kachin communities, featuring sacred manau poles decorated with diamond symbols and curved lines.
The manau leader wears a traditional headdress decorated with hornbill feathers, and male dancers hold n'htu swords.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Jawa Rumja (Tingli yaw), son of Pawng Yawng, and Lamu madai, who led the first Manau.
Celebrated in northern Myanmar, Yunnan (China), and Arunachal Pradesh (India), with large celebrations in Myitkyina, Laiza, Ruili, and Banmai Samakki in Thailand.
